sources.citation: Vedamanickam, P. Edward. 2023. Solaga/Soliga. In: Linguistic Survey of India - Tamil Nadu, pp. 584-634. New Delhi: Office of the Registrar General, India (Language Division).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 Phonology = 2.1 inventory, 2.2 diphthongs, 2.3 syllable structure, 2.4 contrasts, 2.5 distribution, 2.6 clusters/gemination; no suprasegmental subsection (the volume's '2.8.4 Stress' passage belongs to the Toda chapter). Data from Hasanur village, Sathyamangalam taluk, Erode district, Tamil Nadu.

sources.citation: Mariswamy, R. 2014. Soliga samaajobhashika adhyayana [A sociolinguistic study of Soliga; in Kannada]. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Mysore. Shodhganga hdl 10603/110465.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 sec. 2.1 'Soliga bhasha dhvaniracane' (pp. 55-62) lists Soliga-vs-standard-Kannada sound correspondences plus vowel and consonant charts; no term for stress (ottu / balaghata / svarabhara / aghata) occurs (Kannada scanned of the section, a full-text search for stress/accent + read).

sources.citation: Si, Aung. 2012. The traditional ecological knowledge of the Solega: a linguistic perspective. PhD thesis, Australian National University (xiv+366 leaves; Appendix A 'A Sketch Grammar of Solega', Appendix B lexicon). hdl 1885/149874, doi 10.25911/5d5e75b032ef7.
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix A sec. 1 'Solega Phonology' has only 1.1 phoneme inventory (consonants, vowels incl. length and nasalisation contrasts), 1.2 general comments (orthography), 1.3 processes at morpheme boundaries, 1.4 syllable structure; no stress/accent/prosody statement anywhere in the sketch (a full-text search for stress/accent whole text for stress/accent/prosod/suprasegmental + reading of 1.1.2-1.4). Variety: Five-clan (aidu kula) Solega of the B.R. Hills, Karnataka.

sources.citation: [Anon., after Gurubasave Gowda 1968]. 1996. 'Soliga language'. In: T. Madhava Menon (ed.), The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, vol. II, pp. 322-323. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics.
sources.note: Nothing. One 'Phonology' paragraph: retroflexed central vowel allophones of i, ii, e, ee; retention of two r-sounds; lateral/continuant variation; then morphology. Sole reference: Gowda 1968 thesis.

sources.citation: Mohan Kumar, S. E. 2017. Soliga Kannada: samajobhashika adhyayana [ಸೋಲಿಗ ಕನ್ನಡ : ಸಮಾಜೋಭಾಷಿಕ ಅಧ್ಯಯನ; Soliga Kannada: a sociolinguistic study; in Kannada]. PhD thesis, Kannada Bhashadhyayana Vibhaga, Kannada University, Hampi. c. 217 pp. + appendices (466 scan images). archive.org item kuh.767.moh.132968.
sources.note: A sociolinguistic study; the only sound-system content is ch. 5 'Bhashika parisara' (5.1 speech samples, 5.2 regional-dialect influence, 5.3 age-graded structure, 5.6 'Soliga nudi rachane') and the ch. 6 findings list, which state that nasalization is a distinct phoneme in Soliga (lost in literate 16-35-year-olds) and that Old Kannada ṟ survives as an independent sound; no statement on tone, pitch, stress (svarabhara/balaghata/ottu) or intonation anywhere.

sources.note: The only published linguist's sketch by a Dravidianist who routinely notes stress placement in his Nilgiri sketches (Irula, Jenu Kurumba); 17 pp. with a phonology section; most likely place for an explicit stress sentence.
